t: You're standing where All Hallows Bread Street once stood, on the corner of Bread Street and Watling Street. It was a parish church, first mentioned in the thirteenth century, and it was destroyed in the Great Fire of London in 1666. The rebuilding came from the office of Sir Christopher Wren, who was given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the fire, and who also created St Paul's Cathedral. This replacement church was itself demolished in 1876, so what you see now is only its site.
